html:
The Mountain Métis are a Métis community of the Rocky Mountain foothills of Alberta and British Columbia, around Grande Cache and the upper Athabasca and Smoky rivers. The map places them here in 1492, but the community formed in the 1800s.

Their ancestors included Iroquois and Cree voyageurs and hunters who came west with the North West Company and the Hudson's Bay Company, and who married local Cree and other women. Families trapped and hunted around Jasper House. When Jasper National Park was created in 1907, they were forced out of the park around 1910 and moved north into the foothills. Their neighbours include the Kelly Lake Métis.
